mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the federal funds rate above 5.25% in the current month reduces the present value of expected corporate cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant negative relationship with FEDFUNDS changes (p > 0.05 in OLS).

mechanism_narrative: Rising employment momentum measured by PAYEMS exceeds 150,000 new jobs in a month coincides with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as strong labor demand supports corporate optimism.
failure_condition: Payroll growth above 150,000 is not associated with higher SPX 20-day returns (beta < 0.1, t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in consumer demand proxies like HOUST (units sold) by over 10% in a month creates excess demand that pushes up equity valuations, driving positive 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: No significant positive return for SPX in periods where HOUST exceeds 10% monthly increase (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both INDPRO (industrial production index) and RSAFS (retail sales) by at least 5% in the same month indicates softening supply chains and consumer demand, which elevates risk premia and produces negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: No significant negative return when both INDPRO and RSAFS decline by >5% (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in UNRATE below 4% for three consecutive months suggests labor market weakness that reduces growth expectations and drives negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: UNRATE below 4% not associated with negative SPX 60-day returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When monthly PAYEMS growth exceeds 200,000 jobs and UNRATE falls below 5%, it indicates a strong labor market that supports equity risk-taking and positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: No positive return when combined strong labor indicators (PAYEMS >200k, UNRATE <5%) (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in CPIAUCSL above 2% in a month (inflation surprise) coincides with a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return as investors demand higher compensation for risk.
failure_condition: No significant negative return when CPIAUCSL rises >2% (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime shift to supply-side constraints (e.g., persistent GDPC1 < 17000 in quarterly rolling average), S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days tend to be negative as market anticipates production bottlenecks.
failure_condition: No negative returns when GDPC1 remains below 17000 (quarterly avg) (p > 0.05).
